svg.title: Four Gates Before a Bid Leaves the Building
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-05-bid-release-gates; chapter number: 5; chart type: decision_tree; title: Four Gates Before a Bid Leaves the Building; subtitle: Scope, labor, full cost, target margin, then a stress test; caption: Worked bids convert footage and fixture counts into hours, load the wage, divide by one minus the margin, multiply by 4.33 weeks, and survive one extra worker hour per visit.; assumptions note: Gate thresholds are the practitioners' own figures; the 25% to about 13.4% collapse comes from a 20,000 sq ft, three-visit-a-week model priced at $2,800.; note: Sources Commercial Cleaning CEO (IMbK5m7qbY0 at 00:04:42, 00:07:02, 00:10:01); Channel Zero Marketing (Ey7iPjW1uZQ at 00:13:44); Bid & Profit Lab (T-l3Df3Iino at 00:04:10 and 00:04:26).; nodes: gate: G1; question: Is measured footage cut 10-20% for walls and fixed furniture, with toilets and urinals counted as units?; pass next: G2; fail action: Remeasure and recount fixtures; bathroom counts hide one stall or twenty.; gate: G2; question: Is the wage loaded with payroll liabilities, such as a $15 cleaner costing $17.71 an hour?; pass next: G3; fail action: Stack unemployment, FICA and workers comp onto the base wage before pricing.; gate: G3; question: Is price set as cost divided by one minus margin, billed on 4.33 weeks a month?; pass next: G4; fail action: Reprice; using 4 weeks on a $65 twice-weekly visit gives away about $516 a year.; gate: G4; question: Does margin hold with one extra worker hour per visit?; pass next: Send the bid; fail action: Rescope or reprice; one extra hour cut a 25% margin to about 13.4%.

text.title: Four Gates Before a Bid Leaves the Building
text.tspan: Four Gates Before a Bid Leaves the Building

circle.title: gate: G1; question: Is measured footage cut 10-20% for walls and fixed furniture, with toilets and urinals counted as units?; pass next: G2; fail action: Remeasure and recount fixtures; bathroom counts hide one stall or twenty.

gate: G2; question: Is the wage loaded with payroll liabilities, such as a $15 cleaner costing $17.71 an hour?; pass next: G3; fail action: Stack unemployment, FICA and workers comp onto the base wage before pricing.

gate: G3; question: Is price set as cost divided by one minus margin, billed on 4.33 weeks a month?; pass next: G4; fail action: Reprice; using 4 weeks on a $65 twice-weekly visit gives away about $516 a year.
gate: G4; question: Does margin hold with one extra worker hour per visit?; pass next: Send the bid; fail action: Rescope or reprice; one extra hour cut a 25% margin to about 13.4%.

text.title: Assumptions: Gate thresholds are the practitioners' own figures; the 25% to about 13.4% collapse comes from a 20,000 sq ft, three-visit-a-week model priced at $2,800.
